why_relevant: Self-described first fintech community in North Macedonia; publishes ecosystem posts and event notes. Not a formal association with a member directory, so treat as informal ecosystem signal rather than a census.

source_name: АЦИ Македонија — Здружение на финансиски пазари (ACI Macedonia)
why_relevant: Financial-markets professionals association (treasury/dealing community across MK banks) — membership and events map treasury and markets-technology stakeholders.
Bilateral chamber whose membership includes banks, telcos and IT firms; committees and policy events surface digital-economy positions and introduce foreign vendors entering MK.

~40 foreign-capital companies incl. foreign-owned banks; publishes Business and Investment Indicator and holds quarterly government meetings — good for ownership-driven procurement signals and policy asks.

source_name: Стопанска комора на северозападна Македонија (Chamber of Commerce of NW Macedonia)
why_relevant: Second major chamber (Albanian-language business community, Tetovo/Skopje) with its own member base and events — needed for full ecosystem coverage; also publishes in Albanian, a language outside this run's declared set.

source_name: Сојуз на стопански комори на Македонија (Union of Chambers of Commerce)
why_relevant: Third chamber body; separate membership and sector groupings, useful to triangulate actor lists and catch firms absent from mchamber.mk and MASIT.

source_name: biznisregulativa.mk — MASIT chamber profile / regulatory consultation portal
why_relevant: Government-side portal listing chambers and their regulatory input; links association positions to specific draft laws — useful to trace which sector body pushed which digital/payments rule change.
Association LinkedIn feeds announce events, MoUs and working-group outputs faster than the websites, and expose staff/member engagement. Access is restricted for automated collection.

source_name: Digital Bridge & Business ICT Forum (MASIT–SETPE) event series
why_relevant: Concrete example of association-brokered cross-border partnership (MoU between MASIT and the Greek ICT federation SETPE) with B2B matchmaking — exactly the partnership-formation signal this cell exists to catch; participant/partner lists are collectable.
Leading MK business weekly/portal; publishes sector features on bank digitalisation, vendor selections, executive moves and interviews with bank CIO/CEOs that are rarely mirrored in English.

Monthly magazine (founded 1998, publisher Propoint) with long-form interviews of bank and payment-infrastructure executives (e.g. KIBS general manager) and thematic pieces on SEPA and payment services — high analytic value for vendor/partnership context.

Main Albanian-language MK investigative/news portal (Meta.mk network); covers fintech/crypto regulation gaps and digital payment adoption from the Albanian-community angle — signals absent from MK-only press.

source_name: IT.mk Forum — 'ИТ вести од Македонија' / fintech threads
why_relevant: Practitioner forum where MK IT staff (often bank/vendor employees) discuss rollouts, outages, procurement rumours and app quality years before/after press coverage; useful for corroboration and for spotting unannounced vendor changes.

Aggregates virtually all MK media in one place with per-outlet source pages and an archive search; the cheapest way to discover new/unknown MK portals reporting a bank-vendor deal and to monitor all of them at once.

First private MK news agency; consistent, dated coverage of payment-system policy and infrastructure items (SEPA go-live for the state, NBRM digital-channel statistics, Bank of Italy/ECB Western Balkans payment modernisation) — good for anchoring deal timelines.
Pan-regional business network with a dedicated Skopje editorial hub; regional framing of bank M&A, fintech entrants and payment partnerships across ex-YU markets, often naming vendors.

TV-linked MK portal that carries bank press releases nearly verbatim, e.g. the Stopanska Banka–Mastercard payments-digitalisation partnership — useful redundancy when a bank's own newsroom is thin or offline.

Albanian-language MK portal reporting inter-institutional digital-service plans involving banks, the ICT agency (AKSHI/МИОА) and the Ministry of Economy — i.e. public-sector payment integration signals in AL only.

AL-language MK portal carrying bank product/PR items (e.g. Halkbank diaspora remittance and digital banking services) — captures retail-product and remittance-channel launches aimed at the Albanian-speaking and diaspora segment.
Major MK daily with an economy desk; broad-audience coverage of bank fee changes, outages and digital-service launches, and a searchable archive for retrospective deal timelines.
National broadcaster portal; business segments and interviews with bank executives that occasionally disclose system/vendor projects not in written PR.
High-volume MK news portal aggregated by TIME.mk; carries bank and fintech PR plus consumer-facing complaints about outages/fees, an indirect signal on core-system and channel problems.

Export/SME business portal that reported the Development Bank + USAID + Swiss IME contract for a new digital credit-insurance product — donor-funded digital procurement signals that mainstream press underplays.
Kosovo-based AL outlet with a dedicated North Macedonia economy stream; regional AL-language coverage of MK bank and fintech news, useful for cross-checking AL-language deal reports.

source_name: ProCredit Bank MK blog (blog.pcb.mk) — vendor/bank owned media
why_relevant: Bank-owned editorial channel whose digitalisation category functions like trade-press content (digital assistant, 24/7 channels); such bank blogs are frequently the original text that MK portals republish, so they establish the primary date and wording of a launch.
